name: The Restaurant at The Oberoi Cecil
dress_code: smart-casual; full-length trousers and closed shoes for gentlemen
why_it_matters: The Cecil's grand ballroom — built 1884, where the British Raj waltzed — reinvented as a daylight-flooded restaurant under chandeliers, with Shimla Valley views through the original arched windows. Pan-Indian and Himachali plates served by waiters who memorise the dress code.
insider_tip: Book the high tea slot (3-5 pm) rather than dinner — same room, half the bill, and the piano in the adjacent Lounge starts at 4 pm.
signature_address: Chaura Maidan Road, Shimla, Himachal Pradesh 171004

name: The Lounge & Bar (The Oberoi Cecil)
signature_dish: single malt flight with cheese plate
why_it_matters: Skylit lounge at the heart of the Cecil with nightly classical piano performances — Shimla's only piano bar that has actually run continuously since the property reopened. High tea by day, malts and brandy by evening.
insider_tip: Walk in non-residents are welcome but call ahead during peak season (May-Jun, Dec). The piano runs roughly 7-10 pm; cocktails before, brandy after.
signature_address: Chaura Maidan Road, Shimla, Himachal Pradesh 171004

name: Cedar Garden (The Oberoi Cecil)
why_it_matters: The Cecil's outdoor grill garden — smoky tandoors, slow-cooked dham (Himachali wedding feast) and live Himachali folk dance most evenings. The only luxury hotel restaurant in Shimla committed to a regional menu rather than pan-Indian comfort food.
insider_tip: Open 6-9 pm only and weather-dependent — they pull the al fresco service when monsoon rolls in (Jul-Aug) or when temperatures drop below 5°C in winter. Confirm before showing up.
signature_address: Chaura Maidan Road, Shimla, Himachal Pradesh 171004

name: The Restaurant at Wildflower Hall
why_it_matters: The flagship restaurant at Lord Kitchener's old residence (built 1925) — 23 acres of cedar forest at 2,515 m, with a glass conservatory and bonfire-warmed terrace. Indian, Asian and continental served on the only Oberoi terrace where you can see snow on the Pir Panjals.
insider_tip: Sunday brunch is the value entry point — non-resident bookings open up if you call by Friday. The terrace bonfire only fires Oct-Mar; come for that, not the indoor seating.

name: The Cavalry Bar (Wildflower Hall)
signature_dish: single malt with antique bar service
why_it_matters: Antique war memorabilia on the walls (Lord Kitchener was Commander-in-Chief of the British army when he lived here), leather stools at the bar, silk sofas around the fireplace. The most photographed bar in Himachal — and one of the few in Shimla open until midnight.
insider_tip: Non-residents pay a minimum cover during peak season but it gets waived if you eat at The Restaurant first. Sit at the fireplace cluster, not the bar stools — that's where the silence is.

name: WelcomCafe Cedar (Welcomhotel by ITC)
why_it_matters: ITC Hotels' Shimla outpost (rebranded from Fortune Select Cedar Trail) sits 20 minutes from the Mall on the Naldhera golf road. Large private terrace overlooking the Pir Panjals, ITC's polished standards on Indian, oriental and continental — vegan and gluten-free options handled without drama.
insider_tip: Order off the Himachali specials section — siddu, chha gosht, babru — which the kitchen does on its own (not the buffet line). Brunch buffet (Sun) is the easiest non-resident entry.
signature_address: Village Patengali, Tarapur, Naldhera Golf Course Road, Mashobra, Shimla, Himachal Pradesh 171007

name: Eighteen71 Cookhouse & Bar
why_it_matters: Named for 1871 — the year Willow Banks was built by James Craddock, 'architect of Shimla'. Opened 2016, ranked #10 of 165 Shimla restaurants on TripAdvisor. Menu reads like a cross-India tour: Bengali curries, Parsi dhansak, Chettinad, Mughlai. Live music most nights.
insider_tip: It's the highest-rated full-service restaurant on Mall Road by some margin — book the window table for valley views. Lunch (1:30-3:30) is the same kitchen at half the dinner crowd.
signature_address: Hotel Willow Banks, The Mall, Shimla, Himachal Pradesh 171001

name: The Dining Hall (Clarkes Hotel)
why_it_matters: Pillarless Raj-era dining hall built in 1898 — one of the oldest continuously operating restaurants in north India. Same room since the 1898 opening, panoramic forest views, the British high-tea ritual still on the menu.
insider_tip: Order the english breakfast even at dinner — the kitchen has been making it the same way since the original Clarke family ran the place. The Lounge Bar one floor below pours a decent Old Monk for a fraction of Cecil prices.
signature_address: The Mall Road, Shimla, Himachal Pradesh 171001

name: Cafe Sol (Hotel Combermere)
area: Hotel Combermere, opposite Tourism Lift, The Mall
why_it_matters: The Mall's only proper Italian-leaning kitchen, set in a hotel directly above the Tourism Lift — meaning you can roll in straight from Lower Bazaar without the Mall climb. Multi-cuisine but the pizza oven and pasta are the actual reasons to come.
insider_tip: Skip the Mexican/Thai sections — the kitchen is honest but stretched. Pizza, pasta, the trout grill and the desserts are where it shines. The terrace with the Christ Church view fills first.
signature_address: Hotel Combermere, Opposite Tourism Lift, The Mall, Shimla, Himachal Pradesh 171001

name: Alaya (Radisson Hotel Kufri Shimla)
why_it_matters: Radisson's Kufri-edge property — closer to the snow than any other 5-star in the Shimla cluster. Alaya runs live cooking stations and a regional-flavours focus, including Himachali specials the bigger Shimla hotels treat as token. The Living Room bar pours bespoke cocktails alongside.
insider_tip: Drive up just for the buffet brunch on a clear December morning — Kufri snow viewpoint is 5 minutes further on foot. Vegan and gluten-free options are flagged on the menu, not retrofitted on request.
signature_address: Kufri-Shimla Road, Kufri, Shimla, Himachal Pradesh 171012
